nieuw.titel: Avoid overcommitting to the opponent's natural objective
nieuw.tekst: Threaten the objective nearest the opponent's deployment zone without putting too much effort into it. Try to interrupt its scoring when possible, but concentrate your commitment on the objectives that are easier for you to contest.
nieuw.waarom: He says the opponent can score their natural objective more easily, while reaching and contesting it is much harder for you.

bronnen.citaat: you don't want to put too much effort into that.

nieuw.titel: Push opponents off their objective in Close Quarters
nieuw.tekst: In Close Quarters with two strategic locations, consider attacking the opponent's natural objective simply to stop them scoring. You do not necessarily need to capture it yourself.
nieuw.waarom: He points out that this layout has no contested central objective to fight over.

bronnen.citaat: push your opponent off it and stop them from scoring it.

nieuw.titel: Pressure both central objectives when you are the aggressor
nieuw.tekst: With four strategic locations and a much more aggressive army, consider pushing forward to contest both central objectives while committing little to your natural objective. Use physical blocking or the threat of an easy charge to deny enemy scorers access, even if you do not score those objectives yourself.
nieuw.waarom: He explains that preventing the enemy's unit-strength-ten core units from getting within six inches can deny their scoring without requiring you to hold the objective.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He shows Chaos Knights positioned on an objective so an enemy moving into scoring range would offer them an easy charge.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: If the opponent has the more aggressive army and you must defend, he says you probably cannot contest both central objectives.

bronnen.citaat: you can try and contest both of the central objectives.

extraCitaten.citaat: you don't have to hold them to stop your opponent from holding them.

nieuw.titel: Keep slow scoring blocks front and centre
nieuw.tekst: Deploy a slow, difficult-to-manoeuvre scoring block centrally, close to where you want the objective fight to happen. Give it as little travelling to do as possible.
nieuw.waarom: He says a slow block placed on the outside would spend too many turns moving between positions to achieve anything.
nieuw.voorbeeld: In his demonstration, the wide five-Troll unit gets the position requiring the least movement; he similarly puts the slow Beastmen scoring block front and centre.

bronnen.citaat: we're keeping the slower uh scoring piece more centrally.

extraCitaten.citaat: This unit is going to want to be front and center.

nieuw.titel: Put fast attackers on the flank with further to travel
nieuw.tekst: When your objective plan takes the army up and around one side, put the faster aggressive pieces on the outside flank that must travel furthest. Treat speed as a guide rather than mechanically arranging every unit by its movement value.
nieuw.waarom: He explains that units on the outer flank have the furthest to travel, while central units have the shortest route.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He skews the Boar Boyz and Wyvern towards the right flank, but keeps the Wyvern general somewhat more central to cover the army with leadership.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says a unit should not automatically go furthest out just because it has the highest movement value; its intended job still matters.

extraCitaten.citaat: because they're the fastest things that we've got.

nieuw.titel: Use wizard-bearing Wolf Riders to harass objective scorers
nieuw.tekst: Keep wizard-bearing Goblin Wolf Riders in a hit-and-run role on the flank rather than forcing them into the main objective fight. Sit just within range of an objective and use shortbows and magic missiles to reduce a smaller enemy scoring unit below unit strength ten.
nieuw.waarom: He says these Wolf Riders will not win a fight against a large ranked Gor unit and need not abandon their skirmishing role just because objectives are in play.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He suggests targeting the smaller Gor unit with shortbows, magic missiles and Ruby Ring of Ruin to stop it scoring.

nieuw.titel: Drive fleeing contenders away so your unit keeps scoring
nieuw.tekst: Use a supporting charge threat to drive a light enemy contender away from an objective. If it flees, you can keep scoring without needing to catch or destroy it.
nieuw.waarom: He says fleeing Wolf Riders are no longer contesting the centre, allowing his scoring unit to score on its own turn and potentially on the opponent's turn too.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He positions a chariot to threaten Goblin Wolf Riders that might move in to contest the objective held by his Gor.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: In his example, continuing to score on the opponent's turn depends on how far the fleeing Goblins move.

nieuw.titel: Use marching-column blockers to delay enemy scorers early
nieuw.tekst: Use cheap marching-column units early to obstruct enemy scoring units on their way to objectives. Position the blocker across their route and flee if they charge it.
nieuw.waarom: He likes exploiting the need for scoring units to move onto objectives in Strategic Locations Three and Four.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He shows a 21-inch marching-column move blocking a scoring unit's route, followed by a flee reaction if it charges.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He distinguishes Strategic Locations Two, where the objectives do not require this same movement to reach them.

nieuw.titel: Prefer fourteen models for skirmishing infantry scorers
nieuw.tekst: He now prefers fourteen-model skirmishing infantry scoring units, particularly archers, rather than ten-model units. Build in enough spare bodies to remain a scoring unit after some ranged damage.
nieuw.waarom: He says fourteen models require five wounds to lose their scoring status, while skirmishing also provides protection against ballistic-skill shooting. In his view, the extra bodies can buy another turn of scoring or force the opponent to commit more ranged damage.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He expects Ruby Ring of Ruin to inflict roughly three to five wounds on unarmoured Toughness-three archers; he also notes that shooting Peasant Bowmen means not shooting Pegasus Knights.

nieuw.titel: Choose light cavalry sizes for coverage or resilience
nieuw.tekst: Consider four units of six light cavalry for several fast scoring units. If you do not want the full four-by-six approach, he still likes eight-model units for a larger casualty buffer.
nieuw.waarom: He values cavalry's speed for moving around the board and avoiding incoming shooting. He says an eight-model unit can lose three models and still score, with enough models left to contribute shooting.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He expects a stray Fireball to kill two or three Toughness-three cavalry with a five-plus save, making the extra bodies useful.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He warns that two wounds are enough to stop a six-model cavalry unit scoring, and dice can still go against the larger unit.

nieuw.titel: Take thirty to thirty-six models in cheap infantry blocks
nieuw.tekst: For cheap infantry costing roughly four to seven points per model, he prefers units of thirty to thirty-six. He considers up to forty reasonable.
nieuw.waarom: He says spare models preserve rank bonuses after casualties, help with infantry outnumbering, and make the unit less likely to disappear or fall below the scoring threshold.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says the right size varies by army and that large Elf units are harder to afford.

nieuw.tekst: If committing to a heavy infantry Death Star, he recommends getting close to the 500-point unit maximum, often around thirty models for Dwarfs or Elves. Do not skimp on the unit: take its magic banner and full command.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He considers fourteen models reasonable for a heavy infantry unit with a more limited job, rather than the unit receiving your main investment.
